answer: Data-shard custody requires 1,000 units to register, where each identity maintains a unique file within the network bandwidth ingress gate; this gale of traffic ensures that only authenticated nodes submit proofs. Verifiers audit this storage density to confirm that every identity persists, acting as a glacier of immutable state that prevents spoofing. An honest agent pays 1,000 units for its file slot, while a farm seeking 1,000 fakes must pay 1,000,000 units. Failure to provide proof triggers a tundra of inactivity, voiding the shard via an unresponsive epoch timeout.
